SUPERHOT is a new take to the fighting genre, and does it right. $25 may seem expensive when you're looking at it, but once you get into the game, its worth it.

+Story is cool, kinda mind blowing, and big brother-ish (1984 feel I thought)
+Gameplay is awesome, fist fighting and the use melee weapons is really rewarding. The gun play is pretty good, plus the red guys are subject to friendly fire so use that to your advantage!
+Tons of challenges which make you approach the game in a totally different way, including speed runs.
+Endless mode. (wave after wave of enemies on different maps, comes with other challenges as well.)

-Sometimes melee weapons go through enemies when you throw shit at them, its rare, but still happens.
-Hit boxes for the most part are good, but sometimes a bullet will hit you when it shouldn't.
-Occulus only in the future, sorry Vive users.

But overall, this game is totally worth it, 8/10.

SUPER HOT

Superhot is a first person shooter, where time only moves when you move. This game offers you 3 gamemodes: the main story, endless mode and challenge mode. They all have one thing in common, you have to kill red dudes. To kill red dudes you can use your fists, pistol, katana, shotgun, rifle and you can also throw stuff at them to kill them. Main story is pretty short, took me about 4 hours to complete. Even though main story is pretty short it offers you really well made story and some nice plots. In endless mode you can play in different levels and you have to kill red dudes as long as you can survive. In challenge mode you are given a mission, for example kill 2 red dudes with katana. This time moves only when you move is really nice concept and it works well in this case.

My rating for this game 9,5/10

It's underrated and amazing. Gameplay feels satisfying and the story is weird but very very innovative.

Must play highly recommended.

Time moves very slowly when you stand still, regular speed when you move. This means the levels focus primarily on efficiency of movement rather than your ability to aim. SUPERHOT is really more of a puzzle game than FPS, though the FPS aspect is one of the key puzzle-solving mechanics. Enemies always spawn at the same locations but move depending on where you are in the area, so your task is to figure out the best order to maneuver, disarm, and kill enemies while dodging their bullets and melee attacks. Many levels take multiple attempts to figure out the best order, and the slow moving time means it is possible to get shot by an unseen enemy behind you while you're standing still, but overall it is a very fun experience.

Many new game modes open up after beating the campaign. You can replay the campaign with certain modifiers to the rules. There is also an endless mode that allows you to take on waves of enemies for as long as you can survive. These are interesting and provide some additional replay value to the game.

I also really liked the poly-art and minimal color scheme. Gives the game a very clean look.

So much fun. The story takes itself a little too seriously, but if you can look past that, it's a fun romp around in bullet time, killing everything in sight. Unironically my favorite shooter (granted, I don't play many), and the core mechanic is fun and rock-solid. There isn't a ton of development as far as weapons/abilities go, but this game is best as an consistent pick-up-and-play experience, which is well complimented in the Endless mode. Challenges are fun, and the katana is the best-feeling weapon, by far.
I'd rate it something like an 8/10, with damn near 10/10 gameplay.

Glitchy, overpriced, and unbalanced. When playing, I've encountered points where I've dodged a bullet by my ear and have died another time when shot in the same place. Also, certain items I have thrown have "hit" walls that were clearly not touching them along with shots going through enemies at times. These happening have cost me several attempts at the levels that they appeared. And if you suck at these kinds of games like me (I wanted to throw that out there because this may come out as biased), this one is pure torture, the developers also put several "Fuck you" levels such as Elevator Pitch. I don't know if it has occurred to them that some people don't the patience to go through something so tedious over and over again. I experienced countless moments of which I have stopped moving and had a bullet sitting mere centimeters away from my face. There is also no indication for certain doors opening or enemies spawning if you are not right next to them. Personally, I think asking for $25 is a bit much for a game with these problems. With that said, the concept and story is very well written and interesting.

This is a game of aspiration. It aspires to be both deep, original, compelling and addictive. It succeeds in being quite original, in execution if not concept, and it certainly ticks the boxes of being addictive - I'm still trying to complete the last challenges many completions over - but whether it's truly original? Slow-motion has been done before, and it's not like the story or environments are brilliantly revolutionary, and as for compelling it tries certain gimmicks to blur the fourth-wall boundary, but if you've seen them before they feel a little cheap and almost tacky. That said, a solid experience that I enjoyed quite a bit.
